{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7a889d2ced17c5719a0d6e56763766c6bee51517c68bf648cee0144a83080233","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Turns and intersections: signals, turning lanes, U-turns, right of way and roundabouts","heading":"C — Turns and intersections: turn signals, turning lanes and red-light turns, U-turn bans, stopping and yielding at intersections, and single and multi-lane roundabouts","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Turns and intersections: turn signals, turning lanes and red-light turns, U-turn bans, stopping and yielding at intersections, and single and multi-lane roundabouts
Knowledge domain: how and when to signal, which lane to turn from and into, when a turn on red is legal, where U-turns are banned, who yields at controlled and uncontrolled intersections, and how to drive through roundabouts.

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
A signal is required before you turn, change lanes, leave a roundabout or pull away from a curb, and before any of these moves you check ahead, behind and to the side that it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
When you are moving in traffic, your turn signal must go on at least 100 feet before the turn or lane change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Pulling away from a curb into traffic, keep your signal on long enough that drivers know you are coming into the lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Hand-and-arm signals may be used only in daylight when you can clearly see people and vehicles 1,000 feet away; at night or in poor visibility you must use your signal lights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not use hand-and-arm signals while driving a wide or long vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
The manual shows three hand-and-arm signals: one for a right turn, one for a left turn and one for stopping or slowing down. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Never rely only on another driver's turn signal, because that driver may turn the other way or turn without signaling at all. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A02
Turning rules apply wherever you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
Check for traffic behind and beside you well before you turn, then make the turn smoothly at a lower speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
You may cross a bicycle lane to make a turn, but you must not pull into the bike lane to get ready for the turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
Before turning, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for bicyclists in your blind spot, since riders can come up beside you while you prepare to turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
When turning you must yield to bicyclists in a bike lane or on a sidewalk, and you check the crosswalk and stop for pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
If you arrive at an intersection in the wrong lane for your turn, go on to the next intersection, because circling the block is safer than a last-second lane or direction change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
For a right turn, move as close as you can to the right curb or road edge, and just before entering the intersection look left, ahead, right and left again. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just right of the center line, and Oregon law requires you to yield to oncoming traffic until the turn is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
Make a left turn just before the imaginary center point of the intersection and finish just to the right of the center line of the new street. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
Turning left onto a two-way road against a red light is illegal, and where a left turn lane is provided you must turn from that lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A03
Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the nearest left lane; this turn is allowed on red after you stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A03
Turning from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the side you are turning toward and turn into the nearest lane; this turn is also allowed on red after stopping and yielding. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A03
Turning left from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the lane just right of the center line; this turn may not be made on a red light. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A03
Two or more lanes may turn the same way at once only where lane use signs or pavement markings allow it, and each driver follows the markings and stays in their own lane through the turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A04
The general turning rule is to go from the nearest lane in your direction of travel into the nearest lane in the direction you want to go, without swinging wide or changing lanes during the turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A04
The manual pictures two turning errors: turning into the wrong lane and turning from the wrong lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A04
U-turns are banned at intersections controlled by a traffic signal unless a sign allows the turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A04
U-turns are banned between intersections in a city. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A04
Inside city limits, a U-turn is banned anywhere traffic coming from either direction cannot see your vehicle within 500 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A04
Outside city limits, a U-turn is banned anywhere traffic coming from either direction cannot see your vehicle within 1,000 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A04
U-turns are banned at or on a railroad crossing and anywhere official signs or markings prohibit them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A05
A defensive driver never assumes that a stop sign or traffic signal will make approaching traffic stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A05
At a stop sign, a steady red signal or a flashing red signal, stop before the marked stop line or crosswalk, or if neither is marked, before the unmarked crossing area. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A05
Always yield to vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and bicyclists, and to traffic already in the intersection, when making an allowed turn. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A05
If you cannot see traffic coming from the left and right after stopping, pull forward slightly and scan before going on. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A05
Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless your vehicle has room on the far side. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A05
At a four-way stop, courtesy lets the driver who stopped first go first, and when in doubt you yield to the driver on your right, never assuming others will yield to you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A05
Where two-way stop signs face each other, a driver turning left yields to approaching or oncoming traffic going straight. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A05
At an intersection with no signs or signals, look left first to see that cross traffic is yielding, then ahead and right, and yield to any vehicle already in the intersection or coming from your right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A05
When your road dead-ends into an uncontrolled T intersection, drivers on the through road have the right of way and you must yield to them. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A06
Roundabouts, rotaries and traffic circles are circular intersections with a center island, and traffic always moves counterclockwise around it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A06
A warning sign showing arrows in a circle tells you a circular intersection is ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A06
Approaching a roundabout, slow down, read the signs to find your exit, watch for bicyclists who may merge or use the sidewalk, and stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk in your lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F41 | anchor: A06
To enter a roundabout you yield to traffic already inside and to traffic exiting, wait for a gap, merge, and stay ready to stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F42 | anchor: A06
Inside a roundabout, circle until your exit, give a bicyclist who has merged into traffic the full lane, and never pass a bicyclist within the roundabout. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F43 | anchor: A06
To leave a roundabout, use your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk, ready to stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F44 | anchor: A07
In a multi-lane roundabout, read exit and lane use signs and markings before entering, pick the lane for your exit, keep that lane until you leave and avoid lane changes inside. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-F45 | anchor: A07
Trucks may straddle both lanes of a roundabout, and passing or driving beside a truck inside a roundabout is illegal. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-F46 | anchor: A07
When emergency vehicles are approaching, do not enter the roundabout; pull to the right and let other vehicles clear the intersection. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-F47 | anchor: A07
Never stop inside a roundabout for an emergency vehicle; keep going, exit, and then pull onto the right shoulder to let it pass. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]

Misconceptions: a turn on red is not always banned, since two kinds of turn onto a one-way road are allowed after a full stop and yield; you may cross a bike lane to turn but not drive in it first; being in the wrong lane is fixed at the next intersection, not by a late swerve; the manual calls first-to-stop-goes-first at a four-way stop a courtesy, with yielding to the driver on the right when in doubt, so never assume the other driver will yield; you never stop inside a roundabout for a siren.
Mnemonics: left, ahead, right, left again before any turn; nearest lane to nearest lane; onto a one-way you may go on red, onto a two-way you may not; in a roundabout, yield to get in, go counterclockwise, signal right to get out.
Glossary: roundabout means a circular intersection with a center island and one-way counterclockwise flow; dual turn lanes means two lanes allowed to turn the same direction together; T intersection means a road that ends at a through road; vulnerable road users means pedestrians and bicyclists; straddle means a large truck using both roundabout lanes at once.
Dynamic facts: none in these pages; the signal distance, U-turn visibility distances and red-light turn rules are fixed statements of the current manual.
